transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Ethan (ScalePay CTO), Sofia (Lead Backend), Liu (Data Eng), Avery (PM)
Shared artifacts: Deck: https://redwood.app/share/poc-integration-deck (see slide 7-11), SDK sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples, Benchmark sheet: https://drive.company/scale-pay-benchmarks

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's integration progress, focus on SDK tool/function calling patterns, structured output parsing for downstream accounting flows, and tuning for latency/cost. Identified two integration gaps (retry behavior on partial tool failures; parsing edge-cases for structured output), agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): "All right thanks everyone for hopping on. quick agenda — 1) review the integration run results you sent, 2) go over the SDK function/tool call patterns Diego implemented, 3) structured-output parsing issues Sofia flagged, and 4) next steps. if you want to add anything, go ahead."

[00:28] Ethan (ScalePay): "Thanks Maya. quick call out — the run we posted was the weekend low-load test plus a small spike run. main thing we saw was p95 on the hosted route at about 360ms with batch size 8, but when we tried streaming+tool calls the CPU on the app side spiked, so we had some timeouts."

[01:05] Diego (Redwood SE): "Got it. so two things to check: 1) the SDK default retry/backoff we shipped in the sample is conservative and may re-send in-flight requests if the client doesn't handle idempotency tokens, 2) the tool-call flow currently returns structured JSON in a narrative field and we had some tokenization artifacts — we'll demo the exact payloads in a sec. also note, when you hit the hosted endpoint with streaming + tool calls there is more reordering in the response chunks, that can look like duplication but it's usually chunk reassembly at the transport layer."

[02:10] Sofia (ScalePay): "Yeah we saw duplicates — sometimes the post-processor picked up function outputs twice because of missing unique invocation ids in the sample. also a couple of items where the 'order_total' field came back as the string 'one two three' (transcriptiony) instead of 123. small but caused our downstream ledger to fail strict schema validation."

[03:00] Diego (Redwood): "Right, the sample SDK was using a lightweight serializer; we'll push an update to include a canonical invocation_id in the tool call metadata and make the structured output strict-JSON by default. that should stop your double-processing."

[04:05] Liu (ScalePay): "Quick q on KV cache — you previously suggested prefix caching to reduce tokens for repeated invoice lookups. we implemented a small cache but the hit rate was low; are we doing something wrong?"

[04:33] Diego (Redwood): "Two likely causes: 1) your prompt templates vary client-side (micro-diffs), so prefix keys don't collide; 2) sequence length differences cause kernel selection to change and the cache invalidates. recommended: normalize prompt templates and send a cache_key header (see SDK sample) so Redwood runtime can apply exact-match prefix caching. we'll add that to the example."

[05:10] Avery (ScalePay): "Also on the security side — we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logging for the Dedicated pilot. is that something we can get in the SOW?"

[05:28] Maya (Redwood): "Yes — Dedicated includes customer KMS options and audit log exports. I'll include the security attachment in the SOW. Priya can help coordinate the deeper security call with your infosec."

[06:00] Priya (Redwood CSM): "I'll reach out to schedule the SOC2/ISO deep dive next week. please send over a list of compliance artifacts you'd like to see ahead of time so we can have the right folks there."

[06:30] Ethan (ScalePay): "We'll prepare that. back to SDK — Diego, can you walk through the function calling pattern you suggested for the payments reconciliation flow? we want deterministic outputs we can map to our accounting schema."

[07:05] Diego (Redwood SE): "Sure. high level: we expose two patterns in the SDK — 1) tool-call API where you register named tools (e.g., 'lookup_invoice', 'calculate_tax') and the model returns a function invocation with arguments; 2) structured-output mode where you set a response JSON schema and the model attempts to fill fields. For payments you can combine both: model calls 'lookup_invoice' to fetch canonical invoice, then structured-output fills reconciliation_result with typed fields. sample: call -> {"tool":"lookup_invoice","invocation_id":"abc123","args":{}} then the tool returns canonical invoice JSON, model uses that and returns {"reconciliation_result":{"status":"matched","amount":123.45}}."

[08:10] Sofia (ScalePay): "Two gotchas we saw: 1) the model occasionally returns extra fields not in the schema which our strict parser throws on, 2) null vs empty-string differences — Java strict deserializers choke on that. any SDK helpers?"

[08:45] Diego (Redwood): "Yes — SDK v0.9 has a StructuredOutputParser that will coerce types, drop unknown fields by default (configurable), and emit warnings. we'll show you examples for Node and Python. also will add a 'lenientParsing' flag you can toggle in the call options."

[09:20] Ethan (ScalePay): "Can you share the SDK snippet now? we tried the node sample but it didn't include invocation_id header."

[09:35] Diego (Redwood): "I'll paste link in chat, but tl;dr: set options.invocationId = uuid() and pass options.headers['x-rw-cache-key'] if you want cache control. code: see SDK repo -> examples/app-integration/tool-function-structured-output."

[10:10] [Screen share note: Diego shared SDK repo and pointed to the structured output tests]

[11:00] Avery (ScalePay): "Perf question: if we move to Dedicated pilot, what's the expected improvement for p95 and throughput for our workload? we saw 360ms p95 on hosted — what's realistic?"

[11:30] Diego (Redwood): "Generally Dedicated reduces variability and gives you headroom for batching. with the same model and batch size 8 we expect p95 to drop into 180-240ms range depending on sequence length and whether prefix caching hits. also Dedicated lets you tune kernel selection and use quantized variants if you accept minor quality tradeoffs — that can further reduce latency and cost."

[12:05] Liu (ScalePay): "Are model variants auto-fallbacked if capacity is constrained? we don't want outages mid-batch."

[12:20] Maya (Redwood): "Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants or different capacity tiers per policy. you can configure fallback to hosted or a lower-cost variant. we'll include suggested policies in the SOW."

[12:50] Ethan (ScalePay): "On the tool failures — what should our idempotency model be? if a tool sidecar times out and we retry, could that cause double-charges on payment API?"

[13:10] Diego (Redwood): "Good question. pattern: include an invocation_id and have the tool perform idempotent ops or use idempotency-key in downstream payment calls. SDK will surface invocation_id on tool invocations so your sidecar can check for duplicates."

[14:05] Sofia (ScalePay): "We also noticed the stream unwrap sometimes splits JSON across chunks which broke our streaming parser. is there a recombine helper?"

[14:30] Diego (Redwood): "Yes, SDK stream helper has a 'chunkReassembler' that buffers until a complete JSON object is seen; current sample didn't enable it, that's on us. will push patch."

[15:05] [Small cross-talk; people typing links into chat]

[16:00] Ethan (ScalePay): "On observability: can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route? that'll help us map cost to product features."

[16:20] Priya (Redwood): "Yes — Console provides per-route token breakdown and we can create a dashboard for your routes. also can export traces to your Datadog account if you'd like."

[17:00] Avery (ScalePay): "One more edge-case: structured-output for monetary fields — sometimes model writes '$123.00' with currency symbol. our ledger requires numeric decimals. can parser coerce?"

[17:20] Diego (Redwood): "Parser can run field-level transforms, e.g., strip currency symbols and cast to float. we'll add an example transform for 'currencyToFloat' in the sample JSON schemas."

[18:05] Sofia (ScalePay): "During the weekend test we also saw two 'function failed' errors with 502 on the tool call. traces show a transient DB connection error. what retry semantics do you recommend?"

[18:35] Diego (Redwood): "Retry with exponential backoff and idempotency guard on the tool. SDK's default is 3 tries with jitter; for writes use single-attempt or ensure sidecar dedup logic. also consider making the tool resolve to a read-only check first before write. we'll document."

[19:10] Ethan (ScalePay): "Anything on cost optimization? we want to keep unit cost sub-$0.001 per inference if possible."

[19:30] Maya (Redwood): "Optimize with a mix of prefix/NL cache, batching, and potentially a quantized model for non-critical flows. Redwood Optimize can run an analysis of your request distribution and recommend batching/quant profiles — we can run that as part of the pilot."

[20:05] Liu (ScalePay): "Please run that analysis. I'll upload sample logs."

[20:30] [Diego demonstrates the updated sample flow showing invocation_id and lenientParsing flag]

[22:00] Sofia (ScalePay): "Quick clarification: in structured-output mode, if model cannot populate a field, does it return null or omit? want to be consistent."

[22:20] Diego (Redwood): "Configurable — default will omit unknown or unfilled fields, but you can set a 'fillWithNulls' option to guarantee presence with nulls. we'll add guidance for both."

[23:10] Avery (ScalePay): "Any recommendations for schema evolution? our ledger schema might change; we don't want to break nightly jobs."

[23:35] Diego (Redwood): "Use versioned schemas and include schema_version in the call metadata. SDK can validate against allowed versions and emit regression alerts to Console if outputs start failing evals."

[24:10] Ethan (ScalePay): "About the regression alerts — can we tie to our own prompt test-suite?"

[24:30] Priya (Redwood): "Yes — Redwood has eval hooks so you can upload prompt sets and expected outputs; we'll set up alerts when drift exceeds threshold. good pilot add-on to include."

[25:05] [Short silence while people review the SDK code on screen]

[26:00] Sofia (ScalePay): "One more: we want stricter TLS and mutual auth for Dedicated. is mutual TLS supported for private deployments?"

[26:25] Maya (Redwood): "Yes, mutual TLS and customer controlled HSM/KMS are supported in Private/Dedicated. we'll include config examples in the SOW appendix for your infra team."

[27:05] Diego (Redwood): "Ok let's recap the two integration gaps: 1) add invocation_id and chunk reassembly in SDK to prevent double-processing and stream JSON split issues, 2) structured-output parser improvements (lenient parsing, transforms for currency, optional null filling). We'll push SDK patch and sample updates."

[28:10] Ethan (ScalePay): "Sounds good. timeline?"

[28:25] Diego (Redwood): "I'll push changes and open PR by EOD 2026-08-13, and include Node/Python snippets. Maya will follow up with Dedicated pricing and SOW by 2026-08-18. ScalePay will run integration perf and post results by 2026-08-19."

[29:10] Priya (Redwood): "I'll also schedule the security deep dive for the week of Aug 24 — please send compliance checklist items."

[30:00] Avery (ScalePay): "One last question on fallbacks: if we set fallback to hosted and there's a variant mismatch, will structured-output still be compatible?"

[30:20] Diego (Redwood): "You can pin schema versions and have runtime do runtime normalization — but there's risk of subtle differences. recommend validating outputs in a canary route first and using automatic rollback on eval regressions."

[31:00] [Diego posts link to updated sample repo branch in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/142]

[31:35] Ethan (ScalePay): "Thanks we'll pull it. any other blockers?"

[32:00] Sofia (ScalePay): "Just the retry/idempotency stuff and parser transforms — both look addressable. also want the sample to include a simple sidecar example for payment idempotency."

[32:25] Diego (Redwood): "Will add sidecar example. also include a small docker-compose so you can run locally with mock tools."

[33:00] [Short status update from ScalePay on feature priorities — PM/Engineering sync]

[34:00] Maya (Redwood): "Ok final recap for notes: Diego will update SDK and examples (invocation_id, chunkReassembler, lenientParsing, currencyToFloat transform) and open PR by 8/13; ScalePay runs perf tests by 8/19 and posts results; Maya to send Dedicated pricing + SOW by 8/18; Priya to schedule security deep dive the week of 8/24. any edits?"

[34:35] Ethan (ScalePay): "Looks right. can you also add an example of the invocation payload we should log for audits?"

[34:50] Diego (Redwood): "Yes, will add an audit payload example to the repo and SOW appendix."

[35:20] [Wrap-up small talk: next meeting schedule — weekly cadence remains] 

[36:00] Maya (Redwood): "Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with the links and the PR. Priya will get the security scheduling thread started. see you next week."

[36:20] Ethan (ScalePay): "Thanks all."

End of transcript.
